Done. There's a single acceptance test class, and it passes.

## Summary

The business-day rule for the registration date already rolled weekend dates forward (in `BusinessDayAdjuster.toBusinessDay`) but ignored public holidays. I extended `BusinessDayAdjuster` so the same roll-forward loop also skips the five fixed public holidays.

Changes in `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/BusinessDayAdjuster.java`:
- Added a `PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` set (`2026-01-01`, `2026-01-26`, `2026-04-25`, `2026-12-25`, `2026-12-28`).
- Extracted an `isBusinessDay` helper that treats Saturdays, Sundays, and listed holidays as non-business days, and drove the existing roll-forward loop from it — so when the adjusted date lands on a holiday it advances to the next non-holiday weekday.

The logic stays in the one class already responsible for business-day adjustment; the single existing caller (`OwnerRestControllerV1`) and its test data (the `HOLIDAYS`/`toBusinessDay` ground truth in `AcceptanceBase`) already expected this behavior. `./mvnw test` → **BUILD SUCCESS** (1 test, 0 failures).
